title: Measure sync activity without advancing the signals watermark
answers: Why does a quiet warehouse source appear to have stopped syncing?
Which timestamp tells us when a schema last ran?
Can an empty sync advance last_synced_at?
body:
Symptom: A warehouse source keeps syncing on schedule but is reported as stopped and receives an unnecessary schedule repair.
Root cause: products/warehouse_sources/backend/stalled_schedules.py:stalled_schema_queryset previously measured silence using only last_synced_at, which stays unchanged on zero-row v3 runs.
Fix pattern: Use the later of last_synced_at and the usable last_full_run_at for run activity, as defined by products/warehouse_sources/backend/models/external_data_schema.py:ExternalDataSchema.last_run_at; products/data_warehouse/backend/sync_status.py:_is_stale also consumes this property.
Constraints: Neither stamp alone covers every path: zero-row extraction advances only last_full_run_at, while fast return advances only last_synced_at. Preserve products/warehouse_sources/backend/temporal/data_imports/pipelines/pipeline_v3/pipeline.py:PipelineV3._stamp_full_run leaving last_synced_at untouched, because advancing the signals watermark can exclude late-arriving rows from subsequent signals.
applies: Warehouse schema run-health and stale-status calculations, and changes to timestamp writes on empty extraction or fast-return paths.
